content:
The TAMIU Alumni Association has launched a community donation drive to stock the university's pantry with food and everyday essentials for students facing food and financial insecurity, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The "Pack the Pantry" drive, organized alongside the TAMIU Office of Student Affairs, kicked off Monday, Oct. 19, and runs through Nov. 14. Nine drop-off sites across Laredo are accepting donations: Student Affairs at 5201 University Blvd. (STC 226), the Alumni Office (KLM 261), Jett Bowl North, Pla-Mor, the Sames Auto Arena, 550 Pizzeria, the Lollipop Learning Center, Laredo Title & Abstract, and the Webb County Treasurer's Office.

Organizers are seeking nonperishable foods — dry beans and legumes, dehydrated mashed potatoes, cereal, peanut butter, canned chili, canned fruits and vegetables, soup, pasta sauce, cooking oil, rice, and more — as well as hygiene and household items including toothpaste, toothbrushes, deodorant, shampoo and conditioner, feminine hygiene products, diapers and wipes, baby formula, toilet paper, and bottled water.

The drive feeds into Dusty's Food Pantry, TAMIU's on-campus pantry for currently enrolled students — a service that has grown in importance as more students balance classes with tight budgets.

Anyone looking for more information can contact the TAMIU Alumni Association.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times (Oct. 20, 2026).
